envExample: # Example environment configuration # Copy this file to .env and adjust values for your environment. # PostgreSQL Configuration POSTGRES_USER=postgres POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres POSTGRES_DB=open-mercato POSTGRES_PORT=5432 # PostgreSQL connection string (required) DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/open-mercato # JWT secret for auth tokens (required). # Development-only placeholder: generate a real one with `openssl rand -hex 32` before deploying. # In production the app refuses to start when this is missing, shorter than 32 characters, or a # known placeholder. Docker: set it in the .env next to the compose file, not here. JWT_SECRET=change-me-dev-secret # Migration window for tokens signed before the audience-derived scheme. Raw-secret verification # stays disabled unless JWT_LEGACY_CUTOVER_AT is a valid future ISO-8601 instant; when enabled, # JWT_LEGACY_GRACE_MINUTES also caps each token's age. Use 0 on a fresh install. # JWT_LEGACY_GRACE_MINUTES=480 # JWT_LEGACY_CUTOVER_AT= # Session/cookie signing secret used by auth flows and checkout password sessions. # Preferred over JWT_SECRET when set. AUTH_SECRET=change-me-dev-auth-secret # Optional alias used by some NextAuth/Auth.js setups. NEXTAUTH_SECRET= # When none of AUTH_TOKEN_SECRET/AUTH_SECRET/NEXTAUTH_SECRET/JWT_SECRET is set, session and # password-reset tokens are hashed with a public dev-only key, but only when NODE_ENV is # development or test; any other NODE_ENV (staging, preview, ...) refuses to hash tokens. # Set this to true only to opt a throwaway non-production environment into that insecure key. # Ignored in production. # OM_ALLOW_DEV_AUTH_SECRET=false # Demo autologin (optional; leave blank to disable). # When both email and password are set, visitors landing on the homepage are # signed in automatically with these credentials and dropped into the app — # handy for demos with a single superadmin + tenant. NEVER set these in # production. OM_AUTOLOGIN_TENANT is only needed when the same email exists in # more than one tenant. # OM_AUTOLOGIN_EMAIL=superadmin@acme.com # OM_AUTOLOGIN_PASSWORD=secret # OM_AUTOLOGIN_TENANT= # Events transport (choose one) # REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379 # or # EVENTS_REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379 # Outbound system email provider (communications hub) # A provider key alone seeds nothing: the env preset also needs a from-address from # NOTIFICATIONS_EMAIL_FROM / EMAIL_FROM / ADMIN_EMAIL further down this file. With the key but no # from-address the app logs a warning and sends no mail. # SYSTEM_EMAIL_PROVIDER=resend # RESEND_API_KEY= # # Amazon SES outbound email. Only the region, sender and configuration set are per tenant — the AWS # identity itself comes from this instance's default AWS credential chain (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / # AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY below, or the container's IAM role), so every tenant sends from one AWS # account. Use Resend when each tenant must bring its own provider account. # SYSTEM_EMAIL_PROVIDER=ses # AWS_SES_REGION=eu-west-2 # AWS_REGION=eu-west-2 # AWS_SES_CONFIGURATION_SET= # # Optional: pin every tenant-scoped send to one communication channel id instead of resolving the # tenant's own. The channel must belong to the sending organization or be tenant-wide # (organization_id IS NULL); a pinned channel never falls back to the env credentials above. # SYSTEM_EMAIL_CHANNEL_ID= # Public URL used in emails and onboarding flows APP_URL=http://localhost:3000 # Documents realtime collaboration (optional — run `yarn documents:collab`) # All collab vars are optional: leave NEXT_PUBLIC_DOCUMENTS_COLLAB_URL unset to # disable realtime collaboration; the document editor keeps working in # single-user mode. The URL is embedded at app build time; use a # browser-reachable wss:// URL in production. App and sidecar must share the # v2 secret. When DOCUMENTS_COLLAB_ALLOWED_ORIGINS is unset, the sidecar trusts # APP_URL / NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL. DOCUMENTS_COLLAB_PORT=4101 DOCUMENTS_COLLAB_REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379 # Required with collaboration Redis in production. Every sidecar replica in one # deployment must share this value, and deployments sharing Redis must use # different values. Allowed: letters, numbers, dot, underscore, colon, dash. DOCUMENTS_COLLAB_REDIS_PREFIX=open-mercato:documents:collab:local # Local development example: ws://localhost:4101. Production runtime ignores a # loopback value and falls back to single-user editing without failing the build. NEXT_PUBLIC_DOCUMENTS_COLLAB_URL= # Optional exact comma-separated browser origins; defaults to APP_URL. DOCUMENTS_COLLAB_ALLOWED_ORIGINS= # Required only when collaboration is enabled; generate a unique high-entropy # value containing at least 32 UTF-8 bytes. The sidecar fails closed when the # secret is missing or too short. DOCUMENTS_COLLAB_JWT_SECRET_V2= # Optional v1 rollout secret; when set it must differ from the v2 secret. # DOCUMENTS_COLLAB_JWT_SECRET= # Standalone sidecars set this to the app root (for example /app in Docker). DOCUMENTS_COLLAB_APP_ROOT=. # Additional trusted origins for app requests that must pass host validation. # APP_URL is required in production for security-sensitive email links. # In dev mode these values also govern the HMR WebSocket (/_next/webpack-hmr): # add your public/reverse-proxy/Tailscale host here so remote dev access works, # then restart the dev server. Non-allowlisted origins are still rejected. # In Docker dev, the value must also be forwarded into the app container. # Example: APP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://admin.example.com,https://ops.example.com # APP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS= # Base URL for customer-portal links embedded in outbound emails (invitations, # magic links, password resets, notification digests). Falls back to # http://localhost:3000 outside production; REQUIRED in production, where # sending a portal email without it fails the request rather than mailing a # localhost link to a real customer. # PLATFORM_PORTAL_BASE_URL=https://portal.your-domain.com # Enable self-service onboarding (default: false) SELF_SERVICE_ONBOARDING_ENABLED=false # Enable Open Mercato demo widgets. The code default when this is unset is # `true` — scaffolds ship it off explicitly, so keep the line rather than # deleting it. To hide just the contact/feedback widget while keeping demo mode # on, set the `ff_om_hide_contact` key in the browser's localStorage: # https://docs.openmercato.com/architecture/configuration-decision-guide#ff-om-hide-contact DEMO_MODE=false # Hide the backend footer status bar (app version + terms/privacy links) (default: false) OM_HIDE_BACKEND_FOOTER=false # Enable enterprise-only optional modules (default: false) # Developer preview is free for local/dev usage. # Production usage requires a commercial enterprise license. # Details: https://github.com/open-mercato/open-mercato/blob/main/packages/enterprise/README.md OM_ENABLE_ENTERPRISE_MODULES=false # Enable enterprise SSO module (default: false) # Requires OM_ENABLE_ENTERPRISE_MODULES=true OM_ENABLE_ENTERPRISE_MODULES_SSO=false # Optional comma-separated HTTPS origins for operator-approved private/on-prem OIDC endpoints. # Every discovery, JWKS, token, and user-info destination is checked independently. # OM_SSO_OIDC_PRIVATE_ORIGIN_ALLOWLIST=https://idp.internal.example:8443 # Enterprise security module (MFA, passkeys, sudo) # Active when enterprise modules are enabled and the security module is installed. # Optional dedicated signing secret for MFA setup tokens. # Falls back to AUTH_JWT_SECRET, AUTH_SECRET, or JWT_SECRET when left blank. # Enable enterprise security module (default: false) # Requires OM_ENABLE_ENTERPRISE_MODULES=true OM_ENABLE_ENTERPRISE_MODULES_SECURITY=false # Enable the enterprise Agent Orchestrator module (default: false) # Requires OM_ENABLE_ENTERPRISE_MODULES=true # File-defined (OpenCode) agents additionally need the `agents` compose profile: # docker compose --profile agents -f docker-compose.fullapp.yml up OM_ENABLE_ENTERPRISE_MODULES_AGENTS=false # Enable the S3-compatible storage provider module (default: false). # When true, `storage_s3` is added to enabledModules in modules.ts and the # Integration Marketplace exposes the "S3 Object Storage" card. # The provider can also be preconfigured from env vars — see the # "S3 Storage Preconfiguration" block at the bottom of this file. OM_ENABLE_STORAGE_S3=false # OM_SECURITY_MFA_SETUP_SECRET=change-me-mfa-setup-secret OM_SECURITY_TOTP_ISSUER=Open Mercato OM_SECURITY_TOTP_WINDOW=1 OM_SECURITY_OTP_EXPIRY_SECONDS=600 OM_SECURITY_OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS=5 OM_SECURITY_SUDO_DEFAULT_TTL=300 OM_SECURITY_SUDO_MAX_TTL=1800 OM_SECURITY_WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME=Open Mercato # Defaults to the hostname from APP_URL / NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL when left blank. OM_SECURITY_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID= OM_SECURITY_RECOVERY_CODE_COUNT=10 # ⚠️ EMERGENCY BREAK-GLASS ONLY — when true, MFA enforcement is DISABLED platform-wide: # all MFA challenges and enrollment redirects are skipped and sudo step-up always falls back # to password. Keep false in normal operation; when enabled the app emits a warn-level # structured log at startup and on every bypassed challenge so the event is auditable. OM_SECURITY_MFA_EMERGENCY_BYPASS=false # Outgoing email sender priority: # 1. NOTIFICATIONS_EMAIL_FROM # 2. EMAIL_FROM # 3. ADMIN_EMAIL NOTIFICATIONS_EMAIL_FROM= EMAIL_FROM= # Admin email to notify about onboarding submissions. # Also used as the final sender fallback when the sender-specific vars above are empty. ADMIN_EMAIL=ops@your-domain.com # UMES DevTools panel (default: true) # Enables the Ctrl+Shift+U keyboard shortcut to open the UMES DevTools panel. # Set to false in production deployments where DevTools should be hidden. NEXT_PUBLIC_UMES_DEVTOOLS=true # Deals Map view tile source (optional) # The CRM deals "Map" view renders OpenStreetMap raster tiles by default. # Public OSM tiles are fair-use only — point these at a self-hosted or commercial # tile service for production traffic, keeping the attribution accurate. # NEXT_PUBLIC_OM_DEALS_MAP_TILE_URL=https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png # NEXT_PUBLIC_OM_DEALS_MAP_TILE_ATTRIBUTION=© OpenStreetMap contributors # Example checkout pay-page test injections (default: false) # Enables checkout summary/help wrappers used by integration tests only. NEXT_PUBLIC_OM_EXAMPLE_CHECKOUT_TEST_INJECTIONS_ENABLED=false # Public date/time display format overrides (date-fns tokens). # Leave unset, or set to "system", to use the locale-derived default. # Examples: NEXT_PUBLIC_OM_DATE_FORMAT=dd.MM.yyyy # NEXT_PUBLIC_OM_DATE_TIME_FORMAT=dd.MM.yyyy HH:mm # NEXT_PUBLIC_OM_DATE_FORMAT= # NEXT_PUBLIC_OM_DATE_TIME_FORMAT= # Mock payment gateway webhook secret used by the example mock provider. # Required for webhook verification in standalone integration and local test flows. # MOCK_GATEWAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET=open-mercato-mock-dev-webhook-secret # Mock shipping carrier webhook secret used by the example mock carrier adapter. # Required for webhook verification in standalone integration and local test flows. # MOCK_CARRIER_WEBHOOK_SECRET=open-mercato-mock-dev-carrier-webhook-secret # Default raw body limit for public webhook routes that use the global cap. # Payment gateway handlers opt into their own limit per provider registration. # InboxOps inherits this value when set; override only that source with # INBOX_OPS_WEBHOOK_MAX_BODY_BYTES (its legacy fallback is 2 MiB). OM_WEBHOOK_MAX_BODY_BYTES=1048576 # INBOX_OPS_WEBHOOK_MAX_BODY_BYTES=2097152 # Checkout origin allowlist (optional, comma-separated) # Extra origins allowed to submit payments via the public pay-link endpoint. # By default, only the server's own origin (derived from the request URL, # Host, X-Forwarded-Host and X-Forwarded-Proto headers) is accepted. # Use this when the pay page is served from a different domain than the API # (e.g. a custom storefront or CDN domain). # Example: CHECKOUT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://shop.example.com,https://pay.example.com # CHECKOUT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS= # Rate limiting is enabled by default. Auth endpoints (login/signup/reset) # cap at 5–20 requests/minute which is normally fine in dev, but can bite # when running integration tests against a long-lived dev server. Set # OM_INTEGRATION_TEST=true to disable rate limiting globally for test runs. # See: apps/docs/docs/framework/security/rate-limiting.mdx # OM_INTEGRATION_TEST=false # Auto-spawn workers when starting the app (default: true) # Set to false to run workers separately in production AUTO_SPAWN_WORKERS=true # Persistent events are delivered on exactly one path: the bus skips persistent # subscribers inline and the events worker dispatches them (default: true). # The bus reads this value as-is; it never second-guesses whether a worker is # running. The queue is durable, so an emit with no worker yet is delayed, not # lost. Set to false to run persistent subscribers inline instead (the queued job # is stamped, so a worker draining it skips the job - not dual-dispatch). # OM_EVENTS_SINGLE_DELIVERY=true # # `mercato server`/`start` reconciles the value above for a process it KNOWS runs # no worker (AUTO_SPAWN_WORKERS off). Set this to acknowledge an events worker # running out of process, so that bootstrap leaves single-delivery on. # Custom entrypoints (a bare `next start`, a custom server) never run that # bootstrap, so neither variable is rewritten for them. # OM_EVENTS_EXTERNAL_WORKER=true # # Minimum milliseconds between coalesced BROWSER deliveries of one event within # one tenant/organization, for events declared with `broadcastCoalescing: true`. # A bulk writer emitting such an event per record then pays one pg_notify # roundtrip and one SSE fan-out per window instead of per record; the last emit # of a burst is always delivered. Subscribers, webhooks and the queue are never # coalesced. Set to 0 to disable coalescing process-wide and restore per-record # browser delivery. # OM_BROADCAST_COALESCE_INTERVAL_MS=250 # DOM Event Bridge (`GET /api/events/stream`) connection bounds, in milliseconds. # Every open SSE stream re-checks the caller's auth and organization scope on the # revalidation interval and is closed after the maximum age (jittered by +/-15% # per connection) so the browser reconnects through fresh authorization. # Values below 1000 or non-numeric fall back to the defaults shown here. # OM_EVENTS_SSE_AUTH_REVALIDATION_INTERVAL_MS=30000 # OM_EVENTS_SSE_CONNECTION_MAX_AGE_MS=300000 # Dev-mode memory optimization: which workspace packages the `yarn dev` # package watcher tracks. The watcher's memory footprint scales with the # number of watched packages, so narrowing the scope is the main lever for # reducing dev-mode RAM usage. Modes (CLI flag `--watch=` wins over env): # all watch every package (default, unchanged) # auto-optimized watch only packages touched recently (git working tree + # current-branch diff), re-checking every 2 minutes # popular watch only the most frequently changed packages (ranked # from recent git history; capped by OM_WATCH_POPULAR_LIMIT) # env watch exactly the packages listed in OM_WATCH_PACKAGES # The active mode is printed with an emoji at dev startup. # OM_WATCH_SCOPE=all # OM_WATCH_PACKAGES=core,ui,shared # used when OM_WATCH_SCOPE=env # OM_WATCH_POPULAR_LIMIT=6 # cap for OM_WATCH_SCOPE=popular # Dev runtime diagnostics (development only; never enabled in a production build). # The `yarn dev` supervisor collects process, log, warmup, probe and browser # signals into one structured runtime state, shows it on the dev splash, and # mirrors it into an in-app banner through a token-protected local bridge. # OM_DEV_RUNTIME_MODE direct|proxy. `direct` (default) keeps the existing # topology: Next.js owns the public port and the splash # runs on OM_DEV_SPLASH_PORT. `proxy` puts an opt-in # local gateway on the public port instead. # OM_DEV_UPSTREAM_PORT Internal port for the managed Next.js runtime in proxy # mode. Defaults to an auto-selected free loopback port; # must not equal the public application port. # OM_DEV_RUNTIME_MODE=direct # OM_DEV_UPSTREAM_PORT=3111 # # Continuous post-READY health probe against the local `/api/healthz` contract. # The probe never re-runs the login warmup and never logs a success. # OM_DEV_RUNTIME_PROBE_INTERVAL_MS=5000 # OM_DEV_RUNTIME_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS=1500 # must be lower than the interval # OM_DEV_RUNTIME_PROBE_FAILURE_THRESHOLD=3 # consecutive failures -> degraded # OM_DEV_RUNTIME_PROBE_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD=2 # consecutive successes -> ready # # Collection and presentation toggles. Both follow the dev splash by default and # stay off in CI. Turning diagnostics off also disables the in-app banner, and # with it the dev-only status/diagnostics/recovery-action routes. # OM_DEV_RUNTIME_DIAGNOSTICS=true # OM_DEV_RUNTIME_BANNER=true # Base directory for local file-backed queues (default: ./.mercato/queue) QUEUE_BASE_DIR=./.mercato/queue # SSL Certificate Configuration # Path to additional CA certificates for Node.js HTTPS connections # Required for Raiffeisen Bank API which doesn't send complete certificate chain # The GeoTrust EV RSA CA G2 intermediate certificate is needed for SSL verification # Certificate valid until: July 2, 2030 # To update: curl -o certs/geotrust-ev-rsa-ca-g2.pem https://cacerts.digicert.com/GeoTrustEVRSACAG2.crt.pem #NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=./certs/geotrust-ev-rsa-ca-g2.pem # Hybrid query engine SQL logging (optional, default: false) # Set to true to log raw SQL statements from the hybrid query engine. QUERY_ENGINE_DEBUG_SQL=false # Enable tree profiler for matching resources/entities (comma-separated filters, e.g. * - for all profilers,customers.*, customers.people) # OM_PROFILE= # Enable detailed CRUD profiling for matching resources (comma-separated filters, e.g. customers.*, *) # OM_CRUD_PROFILE= # Enable hybrid query engine profiling for matching entities (comma-separated filters, e.g. customers.*, customers.people) # OM_QE_PROFILE= # Enable cache for CRUD API responses (default: false) ENABLE_CRUD_API_CACHE=false # Make query-index read-projection tail synchronous and loud on write (default: false) OM_CACHE_SAFETY_ALWAYS_CONSISTENT=false # Auto-reindex query indexes when coverage gaps are detected (default: true) SCHEDULE_AUTO_REINDEX=true # Collapse repeated auto-reindex scheduling for the same scope (default: 30000 ms; 0 disables) OM_QUERY_INDEX_AUTO_REINDEX_DEBOUNCE_MS=30000 # Skip immediate coverage recalculation on read (default: false) OPTIMIZE_INDEX_COVERAGE_STATS=false # Maximum reported list total (default: 10000). Counting stops after this many # matching rows; capped totals render as "10 000+" and responses carry # totalIsCapped: true. 0 disables capping and restores exact counts everywhere. OM_LIST_COUNT_CAP=10000 # Continue serving results from entity indexes when coverage gaps are detected (default: true) FORCE_QUERY_INDEX_ON_PARTIAL_INDEXES=true # Hashed search tokenization defaults OM_SEARCH_ENABLED=true OM_SEARCH_MIN_LEN=3 OM_SEARCH_ENABLE_PARTIAL=true OM_SEARCH_HASH_ALGO=sha256 OM_SEARCH_STORE_RAW_TOKENS=false # Run like/ilike on PLAINTEXT base columns as SQL ILIKE -- one containment predicate per word of # the term, ANDed -- instead of the approximate search-token match (encrypted columns always keep # the token path). Off by default per #5383, pending making tokenization ILIKE-equivalent. Token # matching drops fragments shorter than OM_SEARCH_MIN_LEN, so a list search for "2026-08" can match # the "2026-01" row instead of the one asked for -- set this to true to opt into the fix ahead of # that follow-up. Per-word ANDing keeps word-order-independent matching when enabled, so # "Warehouse 12" still matches "Warehouse A 12". OM_SEARCH_USE_ILIKE_FOR_NON_ENCRYPTED_FIELDS=false # Bound token fan-out per indexed record (0 disables an individual limit) OM_SEARCH_MAX_FIELD_CHARS=20000 OM_SEARCH_MAX_TOKENS_PER_FIELD=5000 OM_SEARCH_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RECORD=20000 # Optional comma-separated blocklist of field name substrings to skip during tokenization. # Applies to per-field tokens AND to the aggregate `search_text` field, so blocklisting a # large free-text column genuinely keeps it out of the token index. password,token,secret,hash # are always blocked. Prefix an entry with `entityType@` to scope it to one entity type. # OM_SEARCH_FIELD_BLOCKLIST=body,customers:customer_interaction@notes # TTL for the process-level "does this entity have search tokens?" probe cache (ms, 0 disables). OM_SEARCH_TOKEN_PRESENCE_CACHE_MS=30000 # Offer base `customers:customer_entity` rows as search results alongside the person/company # profiles. Off by default: a customer is found through their profile, which is what carries the # detail-page link, so the base row only adds a second, navigation-less copy of the same customer # to global search. Turn it on to restore the previous behavior -- both rows are returned and the # presenter enricher merges the pair back into one canonical result. Read-side only: the rows stay # in search_tokens either way, because the People/Companies list search and the query engines' # encrypted like/ilike rewrite resolve ids through them. OM_SEARCH_CUSTOMERS_INDEX_BASE_ENTITY=false # Search module debug logging (Meilisearch, vector search, reindex operations) OM_SEARCH_DEBUG=false # Query index engine debug logging (search:source-has-tokens, coverage, etc.) OM_QUERY_INDEX_DEBUG=false # Toggle EAV backward compatibility for user-defined entities (custom field values) # When true, DataEngine will also write to custom_field_values on create/update of custom entities. # Default is false: values are only stored in custom_entities_storage. ENTITIES_BACKCOMPAT_EAV_FOR_CUSTOM=false # Cache strategy (default: memory) CACHE_STRATEGY=sqlite # Default TTL in milliseconds (optional) CACHE_TTL=300000 # Max entries retained by the in-memory cache strategy before LRU eviction # (default: 50000). Bounds memory for the process-wide cache singleton. A # non-positive value disables the cap (unbounded — not recommended). #CACHE_MEMORY_MAX_ENTRIES=50000 # The cache service is shared process-wide (a singleton) so cross-request # caches actually hit. Set to off/false to fall back to a per-request cache # instance (legacy behavior). Default: on. #OM_CACHE_SINGLETON=on # TTL in milliseconds for the outbound webhook subscription cache (default: # 60000). 0 disables the cache. With a per-process CACHE_STRATEGY (memory), # use CACHE_STRATEGY=redis or lower this value if multiple instances need # webhook changes to converge promptly. #OM_WEBHOOKS_SUBSCRIPTION_CACHE_TTL_MS=60000 # Redis Configuration #REDIS_PORT=6379 # Redis configuration (for redis strategy) #CACHE_REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379 # SQLite configuration (for sqlite strategy) CACHE_SQLITE_PATH=./.mercato/cache/cache.db # JSON file configuration (for jsonfile strategy) #CACHE_JSON_FILE_PATH=./.mercato/cache/cache.json # Database pooling settings DB_POOL_MIN=5 # Conservative local/dev default. Increase explicitly for higher-concurrency deployments. DB_POOL_MAX=20 DB_POOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT=30000 DB_POOL_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT=60000 # Connection-pinning guards (milliseconds). idle_in_transaction defaults to 120000 in every # environment so a leaked open transaction cannot pin a pool connection forever; set to 0 to disable. #DB_IDLE_IN_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 # Opt-in server-side timeouts. Unset = no timeout (legacy behavior). Set to cap runaway # queries / lock waits so they cannot exhaust the pool. Recommended in production. #DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS=30000 #DB_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS=10000 # Background-worker DB connection budget. `mercato queue worker --all` fits the sum of # per-queue concurrency to this budget (one pooled connection per in-flight job) so workers # cannot starve the request path. Defaults to DB_POOL_MAX. Keep # web_pool_max + worker_pool_max + overhead <= Postgres max_connections. #OM_WORKERS_DB_CONNECTION_BUDGET=20 # Audit log retention windows # Core resources (users, roles) keep access history longer to support investigations. AUDIT_LOGS_CORE_RETENTION_DAYS=7 # Non-core reads rotate aggressively to limit storage. AUDIT_LOGS_NON_CORE_RETENTION_HOURS=8 # Minimum gap between retention sweeps per process. 0 rotates on every write. AUDIT_LOGS_ROTATE_INTERVAL_MS=60000 # Post-migration query-index reindex (enabled by default) # # After every module has migrated, `mercato db migrate` reads the # `queryIndexReindexEntityTypes` declarations exported by the migrations it just # applied and queues one persistent `query_index.reindex` per entity type. A data # migration rewrites columns in raw SQL, so it bypasses the indexer helpers that # would normally refresh `entity_indexes.doc` and `search_tokens`; without this # step those projections keep their pre-migration values permanently. # # The step is non-fatal by construction: an unreachable event bus degrades to # printing the equivalent `mercato query_index rebuild --entity --global` # for an operator to run by hand. Set to `off` only to suppress it entirely -- # migrations still apply, but stale projections must then be rebuilt manually. # OM_MIGRATION_REINDEX=true # Module runtimes (SPEC-072): a module can declare `runtime.ts` to start something # once per process -- a worker loop, a broker subscription, a poller. `mercato # queue worker --all` starts them and stops them on shutdown. # # A start that outlives its timeout is fatal, so a runtime that legitimately needs # longer than the default -- acquiring a lease, waiting on a broker -- would # otherwise leave the worker exiting non-zero on every boot. Raise the start bound # rather than removing the guard. A stop that outlives its bound is logged and the # process exits anyway; raise it for a runtime that genuinely needs longer to # drain. Both are milliseconds; an unusable value is logged and the default used. # OM_MODULE_RUNTIME_START_TIMEOUT_MS=30000 # OM_MODULE_RUNTIME_STOP_TIMEOUT_MS=30000 # Tenant data encryption (enabled by default) TENANT_DATA_ENCRYPTION=yes TENANT_DATA_ENCRYPTION_DEBUG=false # Preferred fallback key when Vault is unavailable (use a strong 32+ char secret) TENANT_DATA_ENCRYPTION_FALLBACK_KEY=dev-tenant-encryption-fallback-key-32chars # Legacy secondary fallback secret (optional) TENANT_DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY= # Dedicated high-entropy pepper used to key lookup hashes (email_hash, external_email_hash, …) # so they cannot be attacked with offline rainbow tables or correlated across installations # (issue #2718). When unset, the encryption fallback/legacy keys above are used; if none are # configured the lookup hash falls back to the legacy unkeyed digest. Never reuse AUTH_SECRET here. LOOKUP_HASH_PEPPER= # HashiCorp Vault configuration (disabled by default in local dev). # Uncomment only if you actually run Vault locally; otherwise the fallback key above # is used immediately. # VAULT_ADDR=http://localhost:8200 # VAULT_TOKEN=dev-only-token # VAULT_KV_PATH=secret/data # Bound per-request deadline for Vault KV reads/writes so a degraded Vault # does not stall encryption/decryption across the platform (default: 1000 ms). # VAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS=1000 # ============================================================================ # AI Providers, OCR, and Vector Search # ============================================================================ # New apps ship with AI providers disabled. The unified AI module reads the # `OM_AI_*` variables below first; the legacy `OPENCODE_*` aliases stay # supported as a backward-compatibility fallback when `OM_AI_*` is unset. # Defaults target OpenAI + `gpt-5-mini` — set `OPENAI_API_KEY` (and any # overrides you want) to enable the AI Assistant. # Docs: # - AI Assistant: https://docs.openmercato.com/framework/ai-assistant/overview # - AI settings: https://docs.openmercato.com/framework/ai-assistant/settings # - Search/vector embeddings: https://docs.openmercato.com/user-guide/search # AI Assistant provider selection (unified). Built-in ids: openai, anthropic, # google, deepinfra, groq, together, fireworks, azure, litellm, ollama, # openrouter, lm-studio. # The legacy `OPENCODE_PROVIDER` is still honored as a fallback when this is unset. OM_AI_PROVIDER=openai # AI Assistant model id. Format: `/` or bare `` # (the dispatcher fills in the provider from OM_AI_PROVIDER). Defaults to # `gpt-5-mini` to pair with `OM_AI_PROVIDER=openai`. Examples: # openai/gpt-5-mini # anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 # deepinfra/zai-org/GLM-5.1 # meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct # meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo OM_AI_MODEL=gpt-5-mini # Per-module overrides (Phase 1 of the per-axis-overrides spec). When set, # they win over the global `OM_AI_PROVIDER` / `OM_AI_MODEL` for the matching # module's agent runs.
